note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received on Tuesday 5 May 1936 and there was no contest in any division: the Unionists nominated for the 21 divisions in which they held majorities and the Nationalists for ten, and the retiring members for the divisions without a nomination were deemed re-elected (Mid-Ulster Mail, 9 May 1936, p. 9; Ulster Herald, 9 May 1936, p. 5). Polling in County Tyrone was fixed for Wednesday 3 June 1936; no poll was needed. The new council first met on Monday 8 June 1936 (Ulster Herald, 13 June 1936, p. 5). The changes printed were Glenlark (Solomon Morris for Daniel M'Crea), Bencran (Fred M'Ivor for J. M'L. Armstrong) and Gortin (H. Miles for John Turner) (Mid-Ulster Mail, 9 May 1936, p. 9; Belfast News-Letter, 6 May 1936, p. 9); the Ulster Herald (9 May 1936, p. 5) adds Patrick Quinn for B. Donaghey and John J. Colhoun for J. A. V. Mitchell. There was no change in Mountjoy West, so the retiring member was re-nominated. Division inferred from the 31 May 1933 return (John Given; Irish News, 19 April 1933, p. 6); the Ulster Herald, 13 June 1936, p. 5 names him on the new council: he was elected to the Joint Cemetery Committee at the first meeting of the new council on 8 June 1936. No co-option, vacancy or by-election in the division was found in the 1936 reports read. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Mountjoy West' to Mountjoy Forest West (19 Nov 2026, w19-merges, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official DED name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): Mountjoy East and Mountjoy West are the short form of the DEDs Mountjoy Forest East and Mountjoy Forest West of Omagh Rural District (the 1911 DED map, 'Mountjoy Forest, East' and 'Mountjoy Forest, West'; the NI DED maps of 1925-39); the DED named Mountjoy alone lies in Dungannon Rural District. No round files both forms of one side, and the same members sit under both: John Johnston (Forest East 1924, 1927, 1933; East 1930, 1936), John Given (Forest West 1924, 1927, 1933; West 1930, 1936), J. K. McCollum (East 1946; Forest East 1949, 1952), W. G. Henderson (West 1946; Forest West 1949; West 1955); the Ulster Herald of 22 April 1939, p. 5, prints the council's 'Mountjoy East' and 'Mountjoy Forest West' nominations side by side. This round was filed as 'Mountjoy West', the spelling of its source, kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (mountjoy-west) answers with a redirect to this one.
